notes.title: Update: ... secrets ... words ... for translation ... pauper!
notes.content:
When we released [i]Heaven's Vault[/i] we thought people might play through the game once, maybe twice to see how the story changes itself around what you do. 

... But players are dedicated. [i]Really[/i] dedicated. And many are on their sixth or seventh play-through - and our language system is giving them translations to crack that are [i]seriously[/i] long.

So today we've released an update specifically to make long translations more fun to play. That means two small changes with big impacts: 

[list]
[*] You can now exit an incomplete translation at any time (no more fussing with little words)
[*] Aliya no longer removes guesses from long, unfinished translations before using them in the story
[/list]

... together, this means even when you're translating something much longer than you can crack, it should feed back into the story in more interesting ways.

We've also expanded the dictionary. ("Increased the level cap".)

Also new in this version:
[list]
[*] confirmation before leaving a moon by walking back to the ship (no more falling off Elboreth by accident)
[*] a significant find for plot-minded people
[*] ... and we've taught a Certain Royal Person a lot more mean words. Enjoy, wretch.
[/list](There's the useful round of typos and fixes; thanks to everyone who reported them.)

The distant past awaits!

notes.title: Translation update!
notes.content:
A new build of Heaven's Vault is now live! This update brings a small but powerful new feature that we'd love your feedback on: building up words from smaller words.

With the update, Aliya can now "guess" a new word if it's made from two words she already knows or has guesses for. So no more getting stuck with words you can read and she can't...

There's also the usual round of minor story fixes and tweaks. 

Meanwhile, here's veteran game design and interactive narrative specialist Zarf [url=http://blog.zarfhome.com/2019/05/heavens-vault-design-ruminations.html]describing Heaven's Vault unique approach to building a story[/url] around your actions entirely on the fly. 

Enjoy!

notes.title: Update - Balancing Tweak, More Ancient
notes.content:
New update to Heaven's Vault is all things that are hard to spot, so here's what you (won't) see on playing:

The big one is the balance: towards the mid-to-late game on some runs, when the map starts to get very broad, we've found the game being a little reluctant to provide the key artefacts that open up new sites to visit. This update tweaks the balance to make key artefacts more frequent if you're looking for somewhere new to explore.

Tl;dr, if in doubt; get a drink with Timor; show your stuff to Tapi; or talk to Huang - we've made them more helpful in tight corners: assuming you can keep them on side, of course...

We've also added:

- more words of Ancient, and some more long phrases, particularly for those into their third / fourth runs

- lots and lots and lots of little story fixes, polish, and specifics. Thanks to everyone who emailed in!

Meanwhile, [url=https://www.theguardian.com/games/2019/may/13/heavens-vault-review-inkle-game]here's the Guardian naming Heaven's Vault as it's Game of the Month for April[/url]:

[i]"...a game of quietly forceful consequence.... the way [b]Heaven’s Vault[/b] builds its sense of meaning and magnitude will stay with you far longer than the latest apocalyptic zombie-popper."[/i]

notes.title: Minor update: ruins and fast travel improvements
notes.content:
Minor update this time, all for space sailors. The big features are:

- [b]Ruins![/b]: you can now stop at a ruin [i]even[/i] if the characters are talking
- [b]Improved fast travel[/b] - Six will now take you *all* the way to any moon you've visited before

Along with some smaller things:

- more robust map UI for selecting and charting courses to ruins
- faster dialogue handing the tiller to Six

... alongside the usual collection of minor story fixes, typos, and tweaks.

Meanwhile, here's Giant Bomb spoilering the first hour (but when you play, all the translations, finds and dialogue will be different, because every game is unique):

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VfL95GrO6Qc

Happy adventuring!

notes.title: Translation Gameplay Upgrade
notes.content:
Today's update to [i]Heaven's Vault[/i] focuses on translation, bringing with it two great features:

* [b]Improved Timeline UI[/b] - dedicated filters in the timeline for finding different types of inscriptions, including a new filter for "Solvable Inscriptions" - translations which are ready to be progressed, or completed. 

* [b]Improved Huang[/b] - Huang can now help you break up complex strings into sub-words, so you can crack the longer, more juicy phrases in the game.

We've also added even more lines for the gigantic book, alongside the usual raft of polishes, tweaks, jokes, extra bits of lore and secrets.

Enjoy!

- Improved Huang - Huang can now help you break up complex strings into sub-words, so you can crack the longer, more juicy phrases in the game.

notes.title: Minor patch
notes.content:
We've pushed a quick update to the game today: fixing a bug which was preventing the story-line that results in the Reunion achievement from triggering. Thanks to the players who helped us track that one down.

Meanwhile, here's a review in [url=https://wireframe.raspberrypi.org/features/heaven%27s-vault-review]UK magazine Wireframe[/url]:

[i]"Look at Vault’s sheer scale; its whole timeline is filled with events both past and present, and wealth of language fragments so big you will want to keep building your vocabulary beyond a single playthrough into the New Game Plus mode. Aliyah and Six can talk about anything and everything, if you choose to, and with everything discovered, you build the picture of a living, breathing world – one you just want to see more of."[/i]

Enjoy!

notes.content:
We've been listening carefully to feedback since the release on Tuesday, and have just released an update:

[list]

[*] Search zones easier to navigate on map
[*] Six no longer misdirects you (oops)
[*] A small number of people have managed to get stuck outside levels as well, and that has been fixed too.
[/list]

Happy Deciphering!
